edition.en: Transcribed by Claude from a scan of the revised edition of Zhimo's Poems (志摩的詩, Crescent Moon Book Co., 1928; 1930 printing) on Wikimedia Commons, and checked against the Wikisource text; written in 1924 and first printed in 1925 as the last of eighteen stanzas, the only one the poet kept in the revised edition.
edition.zh: 据维基共享资源所藏《志摩的诗》修订版（新月书店 1928 年版，1930 年再版）扫描页，由 Claude 校录，并与维基文库本对校；作于 1924 年，1925 年初版时为十八首中的最后一首，修订版只保留了这一首。

basis.en: First published in 1925; the author died in 1931. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1925 年首次发表，作者卒于 1931 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: Five lines kept from a sequence of eighteen that Xu Zhimo wrote on his 1924 journey through Japan with Rabindranath Tagore; when he revised the book he cut all the others. It is here as a small lesson in what a poet chooses to keep. Notice that the whole last line is the Japanese word for goodbye, written in Chinese characters for its sound.
note.zh: 五行诗，出自徐志摩 1924 年陪泰戈尔游历日本时写的十八首组诗；修订诗集时，他删去了其余十七首。收在这里，是作为一小课：诗人选择保留什么。留意最后一整行，只是用汉字记音的日语“再见”。

excerpt.orig: 最是那一低頭的溫柔，像一朵水蓮花不勝涼風的嬌羞，
excerpt.en: Above all, the tenderness of that bowed head, like a water lily too shy for the cool breeze.
excerpt.zh: 最是那一低头的温柔，像一朵水莲花不胜凉风的娇羞，
